name: EM1-1-a-dungeon-offers-the-world-map
note: Mac's sentence, reversed: 'if you open it in a dungeon, the world map would be not accessible'.

name: EM1-3-the-strip-order-is-the-offer-s-reverse
note: The strip walks MAP_SHEETS order; reversing it puts the bay before the streets.

name: EM1-4-a-building-is-read-as-the-town-it-stands-in
note: The order of the flag tests IS the law - a shop in a town would offer the streets.

name: EM1-6-an-unknown-place-opens-blank
note: A map that opens blank is a bug report; the bay is readable from anywhere a player can stand.

name: EM1-7-openOn-obeys-an-ask-the-place-refuses
old: return wanted && sheetAvailable(context, wanted) ? wanted : defaultSheetFor(context);
note: The TravelMap key asking for the bay from inside a crypt would be obeyed.

name: EM1-8-the-slot-asks-the-TABLE-rather-than-what-it-can-ink
note: The narrowing is what keeps a tab from being selected round the back while its sheet does not exist.

name: EM1-9-the-slot-ignores-what-the-window-can-ink
note: A tab that inks nothing is worse than no tab - this is the gate that keeps EM1 from shipping a blank page.

name: EM1-10-a-sheet-forgets-where-it-was-looking
note: A slot that forgets makes the tabs cost something to press.

name: EM1-11-the-remembered-view-is-the-window-s-own-object
note: The window edits its view in place, so a kept reference would follow the live sheet around.

name: EM1-12-a-refused-select-remembers-anyway
old:
if (!ids.includes(sheet) || sheet === live) return false;
      if (currentView) views.set(live, { ...currentView });
new:
if (currentView) views.set(live, { ...currentView });
      if (!ids.includes(sheet) || sheet === live) return false;
note: The player never left, so nothing was left behind.

name: EM1-13-the-toggle-does-not-wrap
old: const next = ids[(((i + step) % ids.length) + ids.length) % ids.length];

name: EM1-14-the-strip-walks-the-TABLE-rather-than-the-slot
note: Then a crypt's strip advertises the door Mac's own sentence closed.

name: EM1-16-a-tab-is-hit-only-on-its-own-ink
old: const i = grabHit(tabs, px, py, STRIP.grab * (layout?.scale ?? 1));
note: A hand-lettered word is a thin target for a mouse and a hopeless one for a thumb.

name: EM1-17-the-hit-box-has-no-bottom
old: if (px < b.x - g || px > b.x + b.w + g || py < b.y - g || py > b.y + b.h + g) continue;
new: if (px < b.x - g || px > b.x + b.w + g || py < b.y - g) continue;
note: The whole column under a tab would stop being map.

name: EM1-18-the-tabs-are-lettered-without-a-halo
note: MAP-FIELD6: the parchment's own cracks are the pen's hue; unhaloed letters tangle with them.

name: EM1-20-the-strip-does-not-scale-with-the-paper
old: return clamp((paperW || STRIP.refPaper) / STRIP.refPaper, STRIP.scaleMin, STRIP.scaleMax);

name: EM1-21-the-strip-scale-is-unbounded
old: return clamp((paperW || STRIP.refPaper) / STRIP.refPaper, STRIP.scaleMin, STRIP.scaleMax);
note: A tiny window must still be hittable and a huge one must not letter the tabs like a headline.

name: EM1-22-the-window-clamps-to-its-own-size-rather-than-the-live-sheet-s
note: A sheet in world units and a sheet in map pixels would share one clamp.

name: EM1-23-the-window-derives-nothing-and-is-always-the-wilderness
note: The context is DERIVED off the host's flags; a constant is a host that forgot.

name: EM1-24-the-window-offers-every-sheet-the-place-does-whether-or-not-it-holds-one
note: This is the mid-flight gate: until EM3/EM4 a town would grow a Town tab that inks nothing.

name: EM1-25-a-click-on-a-tab-also-picks-the-place-under-it
note: A tab's word sits over the sheet's own ink.

name: EM1-26-the-strip-is-never-asked-before-the-sheet
note: Then the tabs are ink nobody can press.

name: EM1-27-switching-a-sheet-keeps-the-old-sheet-s-kept-ink
note: Two sheets whose own keys agree would show the first one's ink under the second one's rule.

name: EM1-28-a-sheet-is-never-told-it-went-up
note: mount() is how a sheet claims the shared chrome it needs.

name: EM1-29-the-window-paints-the-world-rather-than-the-live-sheet
note: The window must never know which sheet is up.

name: EM1-31-the-sheet-s-own-clock-never-runs
note: For the world sheet that clock is SOC6's party poll.

name: EM1-32-the-grab-law-gives-an-overlap-to-the-FIRST-box-not-the-nearest
old: if (d < bestD) { bestD = d; best = i; }
note: THE SEAM BUG, put back. The floor strip's rows sit a gap apart narrower than two grab bands, so first-match handed every press near a seam to the row ABOVE - a player aiming at Floor 1 got Floor 2 every time.

name: EM1-33-the-grab-law-measures-to-the-GROWN-box-rather-than-the-ink
old:
const dx = Math.max(b.x - px, 0, px - (b.x + b.w));
    const dy = Math.max(b.y - py, 0, py - (b.y + b.h));
new:
const dx = Math.max(b.x - g - px, 0, px - (b.x + b.w + g));
    const dy = Math.max(b.y - g - py, 0, py - (b.y + b.h + g));
note: Measuring to the grown box makes every contained point tie at zero, so the first listed wins again - the seam bug by another road.

name: EM1-34-the-floor-strip-writes-its-own-hit-test
old: const i = grabHit(rows, px, py, FLOOR_STRIP.grab * (layout?.scale ?? 1));
new: const i = rows.findIndex((r) => px >= r.x && px <= r.x + r.w && py >= r.y && py <= r.y + r.h);
note: ONE grab law for both inked strips, or the floor strip re-grows the seam bug on its own.
